name: Fathom 0.7.0
body:
This release is about making Fathom run smoothly on the H2's very small amount of memory.
The H2 has 32 MB of RAM, and with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and the network drive all on, earlier
versions left only about 3 MB free. Under load (internet radio while copying music over
Wi-Fi, scrolling through a big library, Bluetooth headphones) that meant audible gaps.

In short:

- **Twice as much free memory**: about 6.5–7 MB with everything on, up from about 3 MB.
- **No more gaps under load**: radio over the wired output or Bluetooth headphones, while
  copying over the network drive or scrolling, played without a single gap in testing.
- **Less work when idle**: the player now uses almost no CPU while paused or with the
  screen off, which should also help the battery.
- **The network drive at full speed** (about 1.2 MB/s), without disturbing the music.

How to install: the [README](https://github.com/raparc0r/fathom-h2#installing), or INSTALL.md in the zip.

## Updating from 0.6.x

**Copy the whole new `sd/` folder over the old files on the card** (USB drive mode works),
not just the player: the kernel (`uImage`), its Wi-Fi modules (`fathom/wifi/modules`) and
two new folders (`fathom/ssh` and `fathom/tools`) have to match. If Wi-Fi says it didn't
start after updating, the modules on the card are from an older version: copy `sd/` again.
The bootloader hasn't changed.

## What changed, in more detail

### More free memory

Most of the H2's memory goes to things that are always there: the Linux kernel, and a small
system that lives entirely in RAM. Both got smaller.

- **A leaner kernel.** Parts the H2 never uses are gone: Ethernet and USB network adapters,
  Chinese filename code pages, extra compression formats, the kernel's symbol table (it
  only makes crash reports prettier) and a few others. That's 1.4 MB more for everything
  else.
- **A smaller system in RAM.** Fathom's core system is loaded into memory at start-up and
  stays there. It went from 3.8 MB to 1.7 MB: a slimmer set of command-line tools, and the
  SSH server and some test tools now load from the card only when they're used. With SSH
  off (the default), that's about 2 MB more.
- **Fewer background programs.** Four programs that weren't needed are gone, logs kept in
  memory now have a size limit, and other services were tuned for small memory.
- **A smaller player.** About 1 MB of unused audio code was left out, and the library's
  cache is handed back when the screen turns off.

### Music comes first

When the H2 is short of memory, Linux makes room by dropping program code it can read
back from the card later. Reading it back takes time, and if the audio has to wait for it,
you hear a gap. The same happens when something else takes the processor at the wrong
moment.

- **Audio gets priority.** The part of the player that decodes and plays music now runs
  ahead of everything else, including the screen, and so does the Bluetooth audio service.
- **Bigger buffers where they help.** Internet radio now buffers about a second of audio
  (it was a fifth of a second), and Bluetooth about three quarters of a second, so a brief
  hiccup elsewhere isn't heard. Files still start instantly.
- **The network drive steps aside.** It runs at the lowest priority, and the music it sends
  no longer fills the memory the player needs. That's why it can run at full speed again.

### Less work when nothing is happening

- **Bluetooth and Wi-Fi stopped polling.** Fathom used to start small programs every two
  seconds to ask whether headphones were connected and how Wi-Fi was doing; 0.6.1 replaced
  most of that (it caused 0.6.0's radio stutter), and now Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and the network
  drive also sleep completely while they're switched off.
- **The screen is only redrawn where something changed**, and not at all while it's off.
  Before, the whole screen was redrawn every second, even in your pocket.
- **Fewer wake-ups.** At rest the player now wakes up about 5–7 times a second instead of
  30–40, and its CPU use while paused is close to zero.

### Smaller things

- Internet radio starts about half a second later than before (it fills its new buffer
  first), and EQ or balance changes on a stream are heard up to a second later.
- The player logs each audio underrun (a gap you'd hear) in `/tmp/fathom-player.log`, to
  help when reporting a problem.
- Typed over SSH, `ssh`, `scp` and the `tiny*` audio tools now run from the card.

## Known issues

Everything in [0.6.0's list](https://github.com/raparc0r/fathom-h2/releases/tag/v0.6.0)
still applies.
